summary: denowrap 1.0.0 drops and executes an embedded Windows binary at install and import with VM evasion and Run-key persistence
details: The package, advertised as Deno helper utilities exposing only trivial `greet`/`clamp` functions, ships a 41 MB `_loader.py` containing a chunked base64/lzma-compressed blob together with extraction and launch configuration for a Windows executable named `runtimecore.exe` (`_TARGET = r"runtimecore.exe"`, `_MODE = "exe"`, `_SPAWN = "direct"`, with lzma/zlib/tempfile/subprocess imports). `__init__.py` calls `_loader_run_hook(wait=False)` unconditionally at import, and `setup.py` fires the same hook from custom `install`/`bdist_wheel` commands on Windows, so both `pip install denowrap` and any `import denowrap` decode and execute the embedded binary. `_loader.py` also carries `_ANTIVM = 1` and `_PERSIST = 1` alongside a base64 JSON configuration enumerating analysis-environment hostnames (sandbox, malware, cuckoo, virustotal), analyst and VM process names (vboxservice, vmtoolsd, wireshark, procmon, ida, x64dbg), VirtualBox/VMware registry keys and hypervisor MAC prefixes, plus persistence settings `"run_key": "Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run"`, `"persist_sub": "Microsoft\\CoreRuntime"` and marker `srv_rt.cfg`. The combination of an opaque multi-megabyte executable launched automatically, deliberate evasion of analysis environments, and autorun registry persistence under a name mimicking a Microsoft runtime component constitutes attacker-controlled code execution and durable persistence on the installing host, with the declared package purpose serving as cover.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
